summary:
Lord Alfred Hayes (1928–2005) was an English professional wrestler, manager and commentator, best known for his work with the World Wrestling Federation from 1982 to 1995. Born in London, he began wrestling in Britain in the late 1950s and later worked in France and North America. He held several regional titles and became known as an aristocratic heel manager before moving into broadcasting.

In the WWF, Hayes appeared as an interviewer, host and commentator, often alongside Vince McMahon, Gorilla Monsoon and Sean Mooney. His measured delivery, Oxford accent and distinctive laugh made him a familiar presence on television and home video.

Hayes retired in 1995 after pay cuts and a serious car accident that led to the amputation of part of his leg. He died at his Texas home in 2005, aged 76. He was inducted into the WWE Hall of Fame’s Legacy Wing in 2018.
